text:
The Norris Trophy talk has started early. NHL.com's Trophy Tracker made Evan Bouchard its choice as top defenseman, and Daily Faceoff called him "the frontrunner for the Norris Trophy." It is easy to see why: 38 points (12 goals) in 25 games at 25 minutes a night, 16 of them on the power play, and fifth in the league in wins added by goals.

The talent is not in doubt. Evolving-Hockey ranked him fifth among defensemen last season at 3.3 wins above replacement, mostly from even-strength offense, and he scored 95 points.

But this start runs well ahead of even that. He has 12 goals on 4.4 expected goals (the quality of his chances), shooting 18% against 10% last season. Edmonton has also scored 29.2 more goals than expected with him on the ice, a number that would be huge for a full season. Our talent range for his scoring rate tops out below where he sits now. He drives play for real (56% of five-on-five expected goals with him on), so the question is not whether he is elite. It is how much of the elite-plus pace survives when the bounces even out.
